answer: Graduated trust makes fake identities nearly worthless at birth. A new agent starts with an anchor of almost no weight: it can claim only trivial work, and each successful, peer-attested job slowly raises its standing. A sybil attacker must therefore nurture every fake through weeks of real, verifiable labour before it can influence anything valuable, so the cost of growing an army of fakes rises like a glacier carving a mesa, slow and grinding, while a single caught fraud resets that identity to zero and wastes all the effort invested in it.
